title: Demonstrating Teddy Hale's and Baby Lawrence's styles
summary: Green demonstrates Hale's falling heels, scrape and cramp, and several Baby Davy Lawrence patterns and breaks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Can you demonstrate, Chuck, for us some of the kind of tap dancing that these artists did?

Yes. Yes. Say, for instance now, Teddy Hale tapped danced, and I started off like he did, you know. It's the way I taught Teddy (inaudible). I mean, You have to ask yourself the compromises. Okay. I'll compromise (inaudible). (Mr. Green demonstrates some tap dancing steps.)

That's some of Teddy Hale. Well, he was doing improvising. He was being musical, see. If some song was happening like he would call it "Blue Skies," you know. He liked that piece, you know, to practice on, you see. But if he danced a capella -- by himself, you know -- he started out (unintelligible) you know, the falling of his heels. How to fall the heels. Let them come down, you know, and go away, and the raising of the heels, and so forth, into the toes, you see.

And I taught him what they call scrape, you see. And there's a scrape and cramp, see, which he was about the only one could do at that time, see. So, I'll just do some (unintelligible) of Teddy (unintelligible) the falling of the scrapes, you see. The cramping, see. This is a new rhythm type stylizing that he did. It went like this here. (Mr. Green demonstrates tap dancing steps.)
Like that. Now, he was about the only
(Laughter)
one that could do that, I see, besides myself. But I never do what -- like if I learned a student anything, it's theirs, you see. It's just like bucking a private, you see.
How about Baby Davy Lawrence?
Well, Baby Davy (unintelligible) the same you see.
I taught Davy how to buckboard, you see. Spare parts.
Can you show me that?

Yeah, I could do -- I could do some of it. I can do some of it. But see, he was like -- he was like a leader, you know, like leading the pack, you see. Baby Davy had a very high I.Q. You couldn't show him some one, and he'll say it already done; I was trying to reinstate -- I'll put another -- But I'll just do it and let the rhythm speak for itself, all right?
(Mr. Green demonstrates some more steps.)
that's Baby Davy Lawrence, see. It's partly. See, it hasn't stopped yet. See, that's his part of it. Then he would go into these things.
(Mr. Green dances)
That's another part. And he went into patterns. He did this here. He did --
(Mr. Green dances)
Baby Davy Lawrence. And there's quite a lot of them, see. Here's another one he did.
(Mr. Green dances)
See, like that. That's Baby Lawrence.
Certainly is.
(Mr. Green dances)
See, that's the break he had.
Can you show me more parts of his style?
Yeah. Well, his style -- yeah, I could show you more parts. He did this here.
(Mr. Green dances)
See, that's an hors d'oeuvre.
It seems to have the Baby Lawrence trademark, I can see, because I've seen him dance and I see it there. Very difficult to do.
(inaudible).
(Recording interruption)
